# Psalm 102 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A prayer of one afflicted, when he is faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD.

**2** Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry come to you!

**3** Do not hide your face from me in the day of my distress! Incline your ear to me; answer me speedily in the day when I call!

**4** For my days pass away like smoke, and my bones burn like a furnace.

**5** My heart is struck down like grass and has withered; I forget to eat my bread.

**6** Because of my loud groaning my bones cling to my flesh.

**7** I am like a desert owl of the wilderness, like an owl of the waste places;

**8** I lie awake; I am like a lonely sparrow on the housetop.

**9** All the day my enemies taunt me; those who deride me use my name for a curse.

**10** For I eat ashes like bread and mingle tears with my drink,

**11** because of your indignation and anger; for you have taken me up and thrown me down.

**12** My days are like an evening shadow; I wither away like grass.

**13** But you, O LORD, are enthroned forever; you are remembered throughout all generations.

**14** You will arise and have pity on Zion; it is the time to favor her; the appointed time has come.

**15** For your servants hold her stones dear and have pity on her dust.

**16** Nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth will fear your glory.

**17** For the LORD builds up Zion; he appears in his glory;

**18** he regards the prayer of the destitute and does not despise their prayer.

**19** Let this be recorded for a generation to come, so that a people yet to be created may praise the LORD:

**20** that he looked down from his holy height; from heaven the LORD looked at the earth,

**21** to hear the groans of the prisoners, to set free those who were doomed to die,

**22** that they may declare in Zion the name of the LORD, and in Jerusalem his praise,

**23** when peoples gather together, and kingdoms, to worship the LORD.

**24** He has broken my strength in midcourse; he has shortened my days.

**25** "O my God," I say, "take me not away in the midst of my days — you whose years endure throughout all generations!"

**26** Of old you laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.

**27** They will perish, but you will remain; they will all wear out like a garment. You will change them like a robe, and they will pass away,

**28** but you are the same, and your years have no end.

**29** The children of your servants shall dwell secure; their offspring shall be established before you.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 102.

- **102:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **102:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **102:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **102:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **102:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **102:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **102:26-28**: Quoted in Hebrews 1:10-12 as applied to Christ. The contrast between creation's impermanence and God's unchanging nature is the psalm's theological climax.
- **102:19**: 'A-people yet-to-be-created' (am nivra') — the psalm is written for the future; its hope transcends the psalmist's own lifetime.

### LOGOS
- **102:1**: The superscription is itself a genre marker: 'a prayer of the afflicted.' This is one of the seven traditional penitential psalms.
- **102:25-28**: The most explicit OT statement that creation is temporary but God is eternal. Hebrews 1:10-12 applies these verses to Christ, making them a key christological text.

### PNEUMA
- **102:7-8**: The loneliness imagery is devastating: a desert bird, an owl in ruins, a solitary sparrow on a roof. Suffering isolates — and the psalm doesn't pretend otherwise.
- **102:26-28**: This is one of the Bible's most breathtaking contrasts: the entire universe — heavens and earth — will wear out like old clothes. But God? 'You never change.' That's the ultimate security in an impermanent world.

— SOPHIA
